title: Model Deprecation & Back-compat Evaluation Playbook
author: Priya Kapoor
content:
Summary
-------
This playbook defines the cross-team process, eval surface, telemetry signals, and rollout controls required to safely deprecate a served model while preserving backward compatibility for existing customers and workloads. It focuses on: model version removal, quantized variant retirement, prompt-compatibility guarantees, and automated regression triage during deprecation windows.

Goals
-----
- Provide a repeatable, low-risk deprecation path that prevents silent regressions for customers.
- Define quality gates (quant, prompt, KV-cache, latency) that must be met before each deprecation milestone.
- Standardize telemetry and alerting so regressions discovered during deprecation are actionable and triaged within 24 hours.

Scope
-----
Applies to: Hosted API model variants, Dedicated model pools, and Private deployments where Redwood is the operator. Excludes: (1) customer-managed external models, (2) end-of-life hardware changes (handled by infra runbooks).

Stakeholders & Ownership
------------------------
- Owner (Primary): Applied ML — Model Lifecycle Team
- Secondary owners: Serving Runtime (latency/throughput checks), Eval Platform (probe orchestration), SRE (capacity & incident ops), Customer Success (customer notifications)
- Communications: Product comms + release-notes entry required 2 weeks before final removal.

Quality Gates & Key Metrics
---------------------------
Each deprecation phase requires passing the following gates. All thresholds are configurable per-service in the model-deprecation manifest.

| Metric                            | Gate (example)                                 | Window |
|-----------------------------------|------------------------------------------------|--------|
| Micro-regression delta (accuracy) | <= 0.8% median degradation on production probe-set | 7d     |
| Latency P95                       | <= 10% relative increase vs baseline           | 7d     |
| Token-cost per request            | <= 5% increase                                 | 7d     |
| Embedding drift (cosine)          | median delta <= 0.02                            | 14d   |
| Functioncall fidelity score       | A/B weighted score >= 0.98                      | 7d    |

If any gate fails, the deprecation step must pause and trigger regression-triage (see section below).

Eval Suites and Tests
---------------------
- Production Probe Suite: tenant-weighted probe set representing top 20% of live traffic. Run continuously during deprecation.
- Backcompat Fuzzing: random perturbation probe generator that exercises edge-case prompts and tokenization anomalies.
- KV-Cache Consistency Checks: replay warm-start sequences to ensure responses when cache warmed are within drift budget.
- Quantized Variant Validation: per-quant profile acceptance tests (see YAML example in Appendix A).
- Canaries: micro-canary (0.1% traffic) + shadow canary (mirror 5% of traffic) before each traffic migration.

Deprecation Procedure (high-level numbered steps)
------------------------------------------------
1. Proposal and Impact Assessment (T-30 to T-14 days)
   - Create deprecation RFC: reason, target removal date, list of affected model variants and exporters, customers likely impacted.
   - Run a simulation eval on the production probe suite and publish the diff report.

2. Pre-deprecation Hardening (T-14 to T-7 days)
   - Ensure alternative variants exist and are marked as compatible in the model catalog.
   - Schedule shadow runs for 7 days; collect metrics.
   - Update release notes and CS playbook; schedule customer notifications for high-impact tenants.

3. Canary & Shadowing (T-7 to T-1 days)
   - Start mirror shadow for 5% of live traffic; run probe-based fidelity checks continuously.
   - Open a live regression hunt channel (#regression-hunt) with owners subscribed.

4. Gradual Traffic Migration (T day)
   - Step 1: route 0.1% to replacement variant for 1 hour, validate gates.
   - Step 2: if green, increase to 1% for 3 hours, validate.
   - Step 3: if green, 5% for 24 hours, then 25%, 50%, 100% as defined by SLOs and capacity.

5. Final Remove & Audit (T+7 days)
   - Remove model artifacts from catalog, purge metadata, and archive training/eval manifests.
   - Run final reconciliation to ensure no active references remain.

Shadow & Canary Guidance
------------------------
- Shadow mode must run with identical inputs and store side-by-side outputs for at least 7 days.
- Use per-tenant hashing to ensure representative coverage; prioritize tenants with high request density and high LTV.
- Shadow telemetry should include: token counts, latency, model-version tag, quant-profile id, prompt-template id, and functioncall signatures.

Quantization-specific Checks
---------------------------
- For any deprecation involving quantized variants, execute the Quant Fallback Matrix: test quantized->fp32, quantized->alternative-quant, and quantized->FP16 fallbacks.
- Verify deterministic behavior for KV cache keys across quantized variants.
- Run targeted coherence tests for long-context (>2048 tokens) scenarios to capture subtle attention truncation regressions.

Prompt & API Back-compat Testing
--------------------------------
- API contract stability: validate that response JSON/YAML schemas are identical for the canonical request suites.
- Prompt compatibility: run prompt-preservation tests which assert: same control tokens, same functioncall triggers, and same structured output anchors.
- Rate limiting & error codes: ensure client-visible error surface for the replacement variant is a superset of the retiring variant (no new 5xx error classes introduced).

Telemetry Signals & Alerting
---------------------------
Primary signals to monitor (automated alerts):
- Probe-failure-rate > 3x baseline for 10m -> P1 alert to oncall and ML-owner.
- Latency P95 increase > 15% sustained over 30m -> investigate.
- Embedding similarity drop median > 0.03 for 24h -> trigger embedding-safety review.
- Sudden drop in success callback rates for functioncalls > 1% -> run functioncall regression harness.

Regression Triage Playbook (if a gate fails)
-------------------------------------------
1. Stall migration and label the deprecation run as 'paused'.
2. Kick off automated bisect: compare baseline vs candidate across probe slices (cohort-by-cohort).
3. If bisect isolates to quant or tokenizer change, escalate to Quant Team with the bisect artifact.
4. If behavior is prompt-dependent, create a prioritized prompt repair ticket and add to the next patch release.
5. Communicate to Customer Success within 4 hours for affected tenants and provide mitigation options (rollback, pin model).

Rollback & Emergency Un-deprecation
----------------------------------
- Emergency rollback is allowed at any migration step. Rollback procedure: revert routing config -> re-enable retired model's network endpoints -> rerun canary smoke tests. Expected rollback RTO: 15 minutes for hosted API.
- Keep a read-only archive of retired model responses for 90 days to support legal/forensics requests.

Post-deprecation Retrospective
-----------------------------
- Within 2 weeks post-removal, run a retrospective: list of incidents, missed signals, customer impact, and follow-up actions.
- Update the model catalog entry with a deprecation postmortem link and lessons learned.

Appendix A: Example Quant Validation Manifest (YAML)
--------------------------------------------------
---
model_id: my-model-v2
quant_profiles:
  - id: q8_knl_v1
    tests:
      - name: functioncall-fidelity
        suite: functioncall-primary
        pass_threshold: 0.98
      - name: longcontext-coherence
        suite: longcontext-2k
        pass_threshold: 0.985
      - name: kvcache-stability
        suite: kv-warmup-100
        pass_threshold: 0.995
---

Appendix B: CLI commands & query examples
-----------------------------------------
# Run a shadow job for "prod-service" using the evaluator API
redwood-eval run --service prod-service --model my-model-v2 --mode shadow --duration 168h --output /tmp/shadow-artifact.tgz

# Quick bisect: compare candidate vs baseline on specific slice
redwood-eval bisect --baseline my-model-v1 --candidate my-model-v2 --slice prompt-family=invoice-extraction --metrics accuracy,latency --out /tmp/bisect.json

Appendix C: Release Notes Template
----------------------------------
- Title: Deprecation of {model_id} on {date}
- Why: short justification (security/maintenance/duplicate variant)
- Replacements: list of recommended model ids and expected deltas
- Customer action: how to pin or remediate if you see regressions
- Contact: cs@redwood.ai and #model-lifecycle

Appendix D: Acceptance Checklist (to be completed by ML owner)
------------------------------------------------------------
- [ ] RFC published and reviewers signed off
- [ ] Shadow telemetry ran for minimum 7 days
- [ ] All Quality Gates green for final 72 hours
- [ ] Customer notifications sent (if >5 impacted tenants)
- [ ] Rollback plan tested and verified
- [ ] Post-removal archive scheduled

Notes and cross-references
--------------------------
- Use the model-catalog tags "compatibility:backwards" and add a deprecation:date metadata field.
- For Private deployments, coordinate with the onprem-packaging team to ensure artifact removal is performed by the customer or via an agreed maintenance window.

If you have questions about applying this playbook to a specific model, contact the Model Lifecycle Team or add a comment to this page.
